blocks.prompt: 8 Given the function \(f(x) = 3^{x}\) and its transformed function \(g(x) = 3^{x - 2} + 1\), draw the graphs of both functions on the same coordinate plane and compare their shapes.
blocks.explanation:
Draw two exponential graphs and compare them.
Plan: read \(g\) as \(f(x - 2) + 1\) (2 right, 1 up), make a table for each, draw both, then compare shape, asymptote, domain and range.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3^{x}\), \(g(x) = 3^{x - 2} + 1\).
To do: draw both graphs on one plane and compare their shapes.
Method: \(g(x) = f(x - 2) + 1\), the general shift \(y = f(x - h) + k\) with \(h = 2\), \(k = 1\).

Asymptotes, domain and range
\[f:\ y = 0,\quad R_{f} = \,]0, \infty[\]
\[g:\ y = 1,\quad R_{g} = \,]1, \infty[\]
Both have domain \(]-\infty, \infty[\).
Why: the shift up by 1 lifts the asymptote and the range by 1; a horizontal shift does not change the domain of all reals.

Compare the shapes
Both are increasing exponential curves of exactly the same shape; \(g\) is \(f\) moved 2 units right and 1 unit up. The curves cross once, where \(3^{x} = 3^{x - 2} + 1\), i.e. \(3^{x} = \frac{9}{8}\), \(x = \log_{3}\frac{9}{8} \approx 0.11\).
Why: a shift changes position only, never shape.
blocks.final_answer: \(g(x) = 3^{x - 2} + 1\) is the graph of \(f(x) = 3^{x}\) shifted 2 units right and 1 unit up: the same shape in a different position (asymptote \(y = 1\) instead of \(y = 0\), range \(]1, \infty[\) instead of \(]0, \infty[\)).

answer_figure.alt: The curves f(x) = 3 to the power x through (0, 1) and (1, 3), and g(x) = 3 to the power (x - 2) plus 1 through (2, 2) and (3, 4), with the dashed horizontal asymptote y = 1 of g; the x-axis is the asymptote of f.
answer_figure.caption: f(x) = 3ˣ and g(x) = 3ˣ⁻² + 1: same shape, g moved 2 right and 1 up
